changelog: The four performance profiles are replaced by specific Neural Rendering settings: the DLSS preset (DLAA, Ultra Quality, Quality, Balanced, Performance or Ultra Performance), the number of passes (1 to 3) and the Neural Rendering resolution (75%, 100% or 125%).

Spatial compression and residual frame generation are now their own switches, with a plain explanation of what each does. Residual frame generation is Experimental and only on RTX 40 and 50 cards with frame generation on.
On RTX 40, 3× to 6× and Dynamic frame generation sit behind a separate Unlock multi-frame generation switch, so 2× works with or without it.
Existing OptiScaler.ini files keep their values on update; Reset setup… offers the new choices and writes them.

configUpdateRules.rationale: Only keys absent from an existing OptiScaler.ini are added, so a tuned config keeps its values. Reset setup… writes the tested baseline with the new Neural Rendering choices.
No ReShade layout change; keep the player's active preset, keybinds and overlay choices.
No Shader Toggler layout change; keep the player's effect groups and keybinds.

spatialCompression.label: Spatial compression
spatialCompression.description: Saves performance by giving the edges of the screen less Neural Rendering detail. The centre is untouched.

residualFg.label: Residual frame generation
residualFg.description: Runs Neural Rendering on every second frame and lets NVIDIA frame generation fill the rest. Faster, but the image arrives one frame late, so motion blur and the HUD can look slightly off.

mfgUnlock.label: Unlock multi-frame generation
mfgUnlock.description: Adds 3× to 6× and Dynamic on RTX 40, which NVIDIA doesn’t officially support. It also works with 2×.
